messages:
olga: deploy-bot reports a canary p95 spike after the v3.6.0 deploy (about 580ms). We have Dedicated customers on the route. Recommend holding auto-revert.

deploy-bot: Alert: p95 > 500ms for 4m on canary. Policy suggests autorevert to 3.5.2.

mark: Hold please. If auto-revert runs it will touch Dedicated. Can we do a canary-only rollback and pin Dedicated?

ops-bot: @olga hold placed: suppressing auto-rollback for 12 minutes. Manual mitigation encouraged.

olga: Plan: 1) rollback canary -> 3.5.2; 2) pin dedicated routes to 3.5.2; 3) brief CS. Who runs commands?

mark: I can run them. Commands below:
``` 
redwoodctl rollout rollback --service=inference --to-version=3.5.2 --slice=canary --reason="post-canary tail latency"
redwoodctl routes pin --route=dedicated-global --version=3.5.2 --note="protect-customer-pinning"
```

deploy-bot: Note: holding auto-rollback suppressed. Manual rollback recommended to minimize customer impact.

mark: Executing canary rollback now.

ops-bot: ACTION: mark started rollback at 2026-04-10T17:09:22Z. Job id: rb-4654321000-x

mark: Canary rollback complete. Running quick smoke.

mark: Smoke: p95 returned to ~140ms, no 502s in canary.

cs: Drafting customer note: "During a canary rollout for v3.6.0 we observed increased latency for a small subset of traffic. We reverted the canary and pinned Dedicated routes to the previous stable version while we investigate. No action required from customers. Follow-up with a post-mortem in 48 hours."

olga: Good. Open a post-mortem ticket, include kernel/runtime traces and the rollback commands. Keep canary pinned for 30m then re-evaluate.

deploy-bot: Manual rollback recorded. Recommend reverting recent kernel selector change in next candidate build.

olga: Closing thread for now. Ping if regression.
